newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip, volume moderate.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip, volume moderate.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended weaker on Wednesday in moderate volume, following a drop in bullion prices during the Tokyo holiday on Tuesday, traders said.
Gold futures prices ranged from four yen to 18 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark April ended down four yen at 1,383 yen per gram.

Activity was dominated by spread trading by trade houses in line with the currency market, as private investors were wary of taking large new positions in the abbreviated week due to Japan's "Golden Week" holidays, traders said.
"Local investors also want to see the reaction of the currency market to U.S. employment data to be released later this week," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $340.15/55 per ounce at 0713 GMT, against $339.70/340.20 in New York on Tuesday.
Platinum and palladium prices drifted sideways after moving lower at the opening.

Trade was directionless amid lingering uncertainty over when Russia will resume PGM exports to Japan, they said. Platinum prices ranged from flat to five yen weaker, with benchmark April ending down five yen at 1,473 yen per gram.
The physical palladium market in Tokyo has been tightening since Russia's suspension of PGM exports, although the platinum market was little affected as the shortage was covered by South Africa.
One trader said a large overhang of short positions in TOCOM palladium futures still held by private investors may limit the downside even if Russia resumes PGM exports to Japan.
Palladium futures ranged from flat to 14 yen per gram lower. Benchmark April was unchanged at 603 yen. Benchmark April silver was down 2.1 yen per 10 grams at 193.1 yen.
